title: "Token Embedding"
description: "A learned vector representation that maps a token ID to a dense numerical space."
term: "Token Embedding"
letter: "T"

## Simple explanation

A token embedding is a list of numbers that represents a token for a
model. During training, these vectors can be adjusted so the model learns
useful patterns from token co-occurrence and task feedback.

## Technical explanation

An embedding layer is commonly a learned matrix indexed by token IDs.
Looking up an ID returns its corresponding vector. Embeddings are often
combined with positional information before being processed by a
Transformer or another sequence model.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Embeddings convert discrete symbols into numeric inputs a neural network
can process. Their dimension, vocabulary, initialization, and training
affect model capacity and memory use.

## How it works

For vocabulary size $V$ and embedding dimension $d$, a table of shape
$V\times d$ stores one vector per token. Input IDs index rows from that
table; gradient-based training updates rows used by the objective.

## Practical example

If a tokenizer maps “cat” to token ID 481, an embedding layer looks up
row 481 and supplies its vector to the model. The same ID must refer to
the same token in the tokenizer and model vocabulary.

## Common misconceptions

- Token embeddings are not necessarily human-interpretable definitions
  of words.
- Tokens with similar embeddings are not guaranteed to be interchangeable
  in every context.
